note: Both sets cover the same core facts (solar altitude 50°, window azimuth 0, the Height = Depth*tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth − window azimuth) algorithm, the one-to-one depth-to-height ratio, the truncated isosceles triangle louver profile, and the 25-degree structural bend), and both are heavily redundant with near-identical claims. Each contains the same recurring errors: the formula is repeatedly truncated to "Cos (solar azimuth)" or garbled into "Depth * azimuth - window azimuth", D*1.2 is misbound as a spacing/depth-to-height ratio rather than the height formula, a 1.2 depth-to-height ratio is asserted against the stated one-to-one ratio, and a fabricated quote ("average of 25-degree structural bend...") invents an "average" condition. A adds one more altered quote (the window-azimuth claim quotes "since the louver azimuth" instead of the source wording and adds a wrong condition) plus a spliced solar-altitude quote, while B's only unique error is the misbound "height to spacing ratio 1.2" and an invented "at 12pm on fall equinox" condition on the azimuth claim; these roughly cancel out, leaving the sets equally faithful.
